newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Smith Barney cites Lucent price.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Smith Barney cites Lucent price.

text.p: -- Smith Barney analyast Anthony Langham downgraded Lucent Technologies Inc to neutral from outperform due in part to the stock's appreciation since Lucent's initial public offering, according to remarks by the analyst obtained by Reuters.

-- He also took issue with what he called "aggressive accounting practices (at least versus competitors' practices), certain sources of earnings, difficulty in getting answers to probing questions, and apparent problems in gross margin."
-- This list of factors led Langham to conclude that "the relative PE (price/earnings) ratio is too high" on Lucent stock, according to the document.
-- "Investors wanting the potential for greater price appreciation should consider switching positions in Lucent to (Telefon AB L.M.) Ericsson," Langham wrote.
-- Among the accounting concerns he pointed to was what he said was the company's practice of booking no reserves for vendor financing risks in its Personal Communications Services (PCS) business.
Also in the PCS business, Lucent averages the cost of goods sold over the life of a contract in reporting results.
"This policy overstates actual realized gross profit in the early stages of these contracts" and could penalize earnings in later stages of the contracts, he said.
Other PCS vendors report actual gross profits realized at the time products ship, Langhan said.
-- Lucent has been aggressive in accounting for some software research and development costs and changed actuarial assumptions for pension and post-retirement accounts, he said.
-- The analyst described how "remarkably frustrated" he had become with the company in attempting to gain information in the 10 months he had spent preparing his report.

-- The analyst's remarks conclude, "We believe a fair multiple would be 21 times forward 12-month earnings" for Lucent. He said Ericsson, his favorite company in the sector, was worthy of a 25 times multiple.
-- At the time he was writing his remarks, Lucent was trading at 24.5 times Langham's 1997 earnings estimate of $2.40 per share. Ericsson was trading at 23 times his 1997 estimate of $1.42, he said.
-- The stock, which fell more than five points at the opening Wednesday, was off 3-1/8 at 55-1/2 by late morning.
-- Lucent officials were not available to respond to the criticisms contained in the security analyst's report.
